task: A user whose password is stored as a bytes value that is not valid UTF-8 cannot log in: make_password()/check_password() with the default PBKDF2 hasher raises UnicodeDecodeError. Has this come up before, what causes it, and how is it handled?
gold: An unnecessary force_str() call on the password in the PBKDF2 hasher raised UnicodeDecodeError on valid non-UTF-8 bytes passwords (a regression)
The fix removes the force_str so bytes passwords are accepted as-is by PBKDF2
The MD5 hasher had a similar issue and now concatenates force_bytes(salt) + force_bytes(password) so bytes are still supported without requiring valid UTF-8

task: On PostgreSQL, a queryset using values() with two lookup paths that end at the same column, plus order_by() and distinct(<fields>), crashes with 'SELECT DISTINCT ON expressions must match initial ORDER BY expressions'. What's going on and how is it fixed?
gold: When two lookup paths resolve to the same column, values() selects that column once per path at different positions; get_distinct() refers to it by expression and PostgreSQL binds an expression to the first position it is selected at, while ORDER BY referred to each selection by its own position, so they did not match
The fix (in the SQL compiler) makes ordering refer to the first position an expression is selected at when distinct fields are used
Annotations take part in that but keep their own alias; raw/extra() selections are left out because equal SQL is not necessarily interchangeable (e.g. volatile extra() selections)

task: After upgrading, one of our models that overrides from_db(cls, db, field_names, values) crashes on every query with a TypeError about an unexpected keyword argument. Is this known, why does it happen, and what does Django do about it now?
gold: The fetch modes feature made all query iteration paths (ModelIterable, RawModelIterable, RelatedPopulator) call Model.from_db() with a fetch_mode keyword argument, which old-signature overrides do not accept
Django now detects once per query (not per row) whether from_db() accepts fetch_mode (or **kwargs) and calls old-style overrides without it
Old-style overrides trigger a RemovedInDjango70Warning asking authors to add the fetch_mode argument

task: A filter(is_active=True) on an indexed BooleanField got much slower on SQLite after an upgrade; EXPLAIN shows the index is not used. Why, and what did Django change?
gold: SQLite (like MySQL and Oracle) has no native boolean type and stores booleans in integer columns, so an index on the column can't be used when the explicit comparison to the boolean literal (= true/1) is omitted; dropping it was a performance regression

The fix restores the explicit exact boolean lookup against literals, generalising the MySQL-only logic (refs #32691) to every backend that lacks native boolean fields via a feature flag, instead of special-casing MySQL, SQLite and Oracle separately
SQLite's planner also can't use the index for WHERE NOT (indexed_bool_field = false), a long-standing separate problem not fixed there

task: django.utils.http.parse_header_parameters has a lot of hand-written parsing. Should we just replace it with the standard library's email.message.Message header parsing?
gold: That simplification was already done (#35440) and then reverted
It was reverted because of a performance regression
The check on the header's maximum length was kept, per Security Team guidance

task: Oracle 23c supports multi-row INSERT ... VALUES. Should bulk_create() on Oracle use it instead of the UNION-of-SELECTs statement?
gold: This was implemented (#35295, a supports_bulk_insert_with_multiple_rows feature for Oracle >= 23) and then reverted
It was reverted because it crashed on Oracle versions newer than 23.3
So Oracle bulk inserts still use the UNION of SELECTs workaround

task: On PostgreSQL, altering a CharField to unique=True can leave redundant indexes (the unique constraint plus the extra _like index). Should the schema editor be changed to stop creating the duplicate index?
gold: A fix for this (#28646, preventing the duplicate index when unique is set to True on PostgreSQL) was committed and then reverted
It was reverted because it caused a crash on Oracle, which does not allow multiple indexes on the same field
The PostgreSQL _like index logic was restored to the simpler earlier conditions

task: In the admin, fields rendered inside a <fieldset> (e.g. radio groups, the usable_password field) are misaligned on Safari. Why, and what is the rule for styling these?
gold: It isn't safe to set display: flex on a <fieldset> because on Safari it interferes with display: block on child divs
The fix removed the flex-container class from the <fieldset> elements (admin/includes/fieldset.html and the change_password template) and adjusted forms.css/responsive.css instead
It was a regression from an earlier admin change (4187da258f)

task: Sending via the SMTP EmailBackend to an address with a non-ASCII local part (e.g. jörg@example.com) raises ValueError instead of sending. Why does Django refuse it, and could that change?
gold: Python versions before 3.15 incorrectly encode non-ASCII email addresses using rfc2047, which results in undeliverable email
The SMTP EmailBackend detects and prevents that by raising ValueError (#35713) as a workaround
Python 3.15 fixes the behaviour (CPython gh-122476); the tests feature-detect the fix in case it is backported

task: What is the default algorithm name and iteration count of Django's default password hasher, and where is it defined?
gold: PBKDF2PasswordHasher with algorithm 'pbkdf2_sha256'
iterations = 1_800_000
Defined in django/contrib/auth/hashers.py
